result:
I added `migrations/003_exports_status_default.sql`. I haven't run it, so it's untested.

It does three things:
1. Sets existing `NULL` statuses to `'queued'`. Without this, step 3 would fail on those rows.
2. Sets the column default to `'queued'`.
3. Sets the column to `NOT NULL`.

I made a new migration instead of editing `001_init.sql`, because databases that already applied 001 wouldn't pick up an edit. A fresh database runs all the migrations in order and ends up with the same schema.

The backfill marks every existing NULL-status export as `queued`, including any that already ran. If you'd rather map those rows to a different status, change the `update` line.

I didn't check `src/exports/sink.ts` to see whether it writes `status` explicitly. If it inserts an explicit `NULL`, that insert will now fail instead of silently storing a NULL.
